entries.label: US
entries.summary: Inward-looking US politics moves toward protectionism.
entries.quote: Amid growing unease in the US about domestic security and economic resilience, policymaking in the Bush administration and Congress is likely to move toward increased protectionism in 2008.

entries.label: Iran
entries.summary: The Iran standoff stays dangerous though strikes are less likely.
entries.quote: The Iran standoff will remain dangerous in 2008, as  the US seeks to impose  sanctions while Iran  pursues aggressive and defiant policies.

entries.label: Iraq
entries.summary: Stalled politics threaten Iraq's central government.
entries.quote: General frustration with the stalled political process in Iraq could jeopardize the future of the country's central government, even if the security situation improves.

entries.label: Terrorism
entries.summary: A mass-casualty attack remains a substantial risk as Al Qaeda regroups.
entries.quote: The risk of a terror attack in 2008 that inflicts mass casualties remains substantial because Al Qaeda and its allied groups have been able to regroup.

entries.label: Pakistan/Afghanistan
entries.summary: Political and security problems and radicalism grow in both countries.
entries.quote: Afghanistan and Pakistan are facing serious political and security problems, and the threat of Islamic radicalism hangs over both countries.

entries.label: Russian foreign policy
entries.summary: The Kremlin acts as a spoiler on international issues.
entries.quote: Increasingly emboldened by Russia's economic growth and political stability, the Kremlin will act as a spoiler on the resolution of key international issues as it seeks to oppose US unilateralism and claim a global role for itself.

entries.label: South Africa
entries.summary: The Mbeki-Zuma split makes South Africa's year difficult.
entries.quote: While the election of Jacob Zuma as president of the ruling  African National Congress (ANC) in December 2007 means that South Africa will  face a difficult, uncertain year, it will largely weather the division between  the government under President Thabo Mbeki, who will stay on as state president  until elections currently scheduled for 2009, and the ruling ANC party under  Zuma.

entries.label: Turkey
entries.summary: The AKP's constitution plan raises instability risk.
entries.quote: Despite the ruling AKP's large parliamentary majority, its controversial plan to introduce a new constitution increases Turkey's risk of political instability and distracts from its bid for EU membership.

entries.label: Energy bottlenecks in Latin America
entries.summary: Underinvestment in oil, gas and power limits Latin American growth.
entries.quote: Energy policy challenges in Latin America could limit future economic growth in the region.

notes: The 2008 list has nine risks ('Top 9 Political Risks for 2008'). Summaries and quotes from the archived publications page; double spaces are as printed. The red-herrings PDF (0801-18Top9RisksRedherrings.pdf) was archived but damaged and could not be read; red-herring labels come from the press release, which lists China, Taiwan, North Korea, Saudi Arabia, Nigeria and Russia's domestic politics.
